column3: The Hebrew repeats “in those days”, uses a singular collective Danite, and says the inheritance had not “fallen” to the tribe.
The Hebrew has a singular clan and describes the men as from their limits or extremities; BSB uses plural “clans” and does not retain the latter phrase.
The last question is “what do you have here?”, rather than explicitly “why are you here?”.
The Hebrew says he was hired and became a priest as separate predicates; BSB makes priesthood the purpose of hiring.
The Hebrew explicitly says “that we may know” and repeats their journey as the way on which they are going; BSB condenses these expressions.
The journey is literally “before the LORD”; BSB interprets this as His watching over it.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not repeat “the men” and has a brief “what of you?”; BSB specifies “What did you find?”.
“Arise” is singular, followed by plural “let us go up”; the hearers are said to be silent, which BSB recasts as a question about failing to act.
The land is literally “broad of both hands”; BSB says “spacious”.
The Hebrew uses a singular collective Danite and the image of being girded with weapons; BSB says “Danites” and “armed”.
The location is “behind” Kiriath-jearim; BSB specifies “west of”. The Hebrew actively says they called the place; BSB uses “is called”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “in these houses”, without explicitly limiting the objects to “one of” them; it also has both “answered” and “said”.
The greeting is literally a question about his welfare.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says the five went up and then entered there; BSB has only going inside.
The image and ephod are not separated by an “and” in the Hebrew expression; BSB lists them separately.
Close to the Hebrew.
The priest’s heart is explicitly glad, and he goes into the midst of the people; BSB leaves out the heart and says “with the people”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The men are called together in a passive form; BSB has active “mobilized”.
The Hebrew asks why Micah has been called together, while BSB makes him the one calling out the company.
The priest has no explicit possessive “my”; BSB supplies one.
The men are “bitter of soul”, and the threatened losses concern his soul and his house’s soul; BSB says “angry” and “lives”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “what Micah made” without explicitly naming idols here, and describes a singular sword as having a mouth; BSB supplies idols and uses plural swords.
The valley belongs to Beth-rehob, rather than simply being near it. The city is “built”, without an explicit rebuilding prefix.
The Hebrew repeats “the name of the city” and Dan’s name; BSB condenses the naming expressions.
The image is singular; BSB has plural “idols”.
